question.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned} & x-2y+z=8 \\  & 2x-3y+2z=14 \\  & 3x-6y+2z=21\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & 8 \\ 2 & -3 & 2 & 14 \\ 3 & -6 & 2 & 21\end{aligned}].
$$

Transforming $M$ to reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & 8 \\ 2 & -3 & 2 & 14 \\ 3 & -6 & 2 & 21\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & 8 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -2 \\ 3 & -6 & 2 & 21\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & 8 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :=(-1){R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & 8 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+2{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\{\begin{aligned} & x=1 \\  & y=-2 \\  & z=3.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the solution $x=1$, $y=-2$ and $z=3.$ Or, in vector form $⟨1,-2,3⟩.$
